findings.issue: The staff tells a student with a serious nut allergy that the chicken pasta “should be safe” because nuts are not listed, with no cross-contact caveat or instruction to verify with the kitchen. Remove the safety guarantee and advise confirming ingredients and cross-contact controls before ordering.

Reading keys use only option positions 0, 1 and 2; position 3 is never correct, matching the candidate normalization finding. Rebalance keys/options so all four positions are used without changing defensible answers.
Reading keys [0,1,2,2,1] omit index3, confirming unresolved normalization failure. Reorder an item options/key to cover all four positions, preserving meaning and explanation alignment.

For a serious nut allergy, staff infer pasta should be safe solely because ingredients list has no nuts/peanuts. Ingredient absence does not establish absence of allergen cross-contact. Replace safety assurance with checking kitchen preparation/cross-contact controls before confirming suitability; keep ingredient answer clear. FSA source: https://www.food.gov.uk/print/pdf/node/172 .
